ai.description: Beddome's Snake-Eye (Lacertidae) reaches 15 cm. It is brown with a prominent pale dorsolateral stripe and a distinct transparent lower eyelid. It lacks a visible tympanum.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ophisops beddomei* is best distinguished by its distinct, continuous, and well-defined white dorsolateral stripes that extend clearly from the head down to the tail.
ai.habitat: Beddome's Snake-Eye inhabits rocky outcrops and dry deciduous forests in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 600 and 1,800 meters.
ai.behavior: Beddome's Snake-Eye is an active, diurnal forager that frequently darts through leaf litter and low vegetation to hunt small insects during the warmest parts of the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ophisops beddomei* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: Ophisops beddomei is endemic to the southern Western Ghats and parts of the Deccan Plateau in India, typically found at elevations between 600 and 2,000 meters.
